title: Adaptive deadline buckets and socket lifecycle advisor for SDK transports
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Customer engineers continue to surface three recurring pain points across Python/TS/Go SDKs: brittle monolithic timeouts that either over-cancel streaming requests or silently inflate tail latency, large numbers of long-lived sockets causing connection churn and resource pressure in our Dedicated fleets, and poor streaming ergonomics when SDKs do not communicate backpressure or retry windows to the runtime. Goal: Design and implement a cross-SDK pattern we call 'adaptive deadline buckets' plus a socket lifecycle advisor that together improve tail latency, reduce socket proliferation, and provide ergonomic defaults for streaming workloads. Scope: - Add a small transport-level API for "deadline buckets" (examples: fast=300ms, normal=2s, long=15s) exposed as named presets in Python/TS/Go SDKs. - Implement client-side hedged retry semantics keyed by bucket and route (hedging window default 20% of bucket). - Introduce a socket lifecycle advisor that recommends/proactively recycles sockets based on observed idle distribution and per-route keep-alive footprints (configurable, opt-out). - Streaming ergonomics: include optional header hints (x-rw-stream-window) to surface preferred chunking/backpressure thresholds; provide language examples and a pattern for graceful stream reconnect with user-visible events. API surface details and examples are in attachments. Design decisions: - Default presets will be conservative to avoid breaking existing customers; we will add telemetry to iterate. - Hedged retries are disabled for idempotency-sensitive routes by default and must be opt-in for streaming writes. - The socket advisor is advisory for SDKs initially (logs + telemetry) and then will flip to automatic recycling behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers only. Acceptance criteria: - Cross-SDK examples (Python/TS/Go) demonstrating deadline bucket usage with streaming and non-streaming calls. - End-to-end benchmark showing 15-25% tail latency reduction p95/p99 on a mixed workload and 10-20% reduction in average open sockets for a Dedicated test fleet. - PRs merged for each SDK, docs page in Console docs, and migration guidance. Rollout plan: 1) Implement in Python SDK and run chaos tests against staging. 2) Parallel implementations in TS and Go with shared test harness. 3) Canary enable socket advisor for 10% of Dedicated customers, monitor telemetry for 2 weeks, then expand. Monitoring & telemetry: break down latency by bucket, hedging frequency, socket recycle events, and number of reconnects per minute. Links to artifacts in attachments. Risks & mitigations: - Incorrect hedging may amplify load; mitigate by rate-limiting hedged retries and disabling by default for heavy-write routes. - Socket recycling could briefly increase reconnections; start advisory mode and gradually tune thresholds.
